title: Autoscaler leader telemetry divergence causing reserved pool headroom drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a customer-facing weekend spike several tenants experienced sustained 429s and elevated tail latency despite apparent headroom in the metrics shown in the console. The autoscaler leader made multiple early scale-down decisions for affected reserved pools, which caused burst exhaustion and a prolonged recovery period. Investigation shows the leader was consuming a divergent telemetry aggregation stream compared to the follower replicas, causing headroom to be underreported and scale decisions to be based on stale inputs.
impact_summary: High impact for 3 enterprise tenants (AcmeHealth, Finora, BrightLaw) across two regions: repeated 429s for short-running chat calls, token-level latency increased to 2–4x P99, and automatic failover to fallback models occurred for some requests. Customer escalations opened (ACME-1245, FIN-987). Estimated lost revenue window: ~4 hours during peak usage.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a synthetic burst load that imitates 500 concurrent short-chat sessions targeted at reserved pools with burst credits near depletion.
2) Force a leader election on the autoscaler (kubectl delete pod of current leader) while keeping telemetry ingestion running.
3) Observe that the newly elected leader picks telemetry shard X that lags ~30s behind aggregated follower stream and issues scale-downs based on stale per-tenant headroom.
4) Verify that token accounting (burst credits) drops to zero and that requests begin to receive 429s until manual headroom reset.
5) Confirm without the leader telemetry divergence the autoscaler maintains headroom and does not prematurely scale down.
root_cause: A combination of (1) a telemetry router change deployed two weeks prior that created multiple aggregation pipelines with slightly different windowing semantics and (2) a race in the autoscaler startup path where the leader could attach to an unnormalized shard. The mismatched windowing caused the leader to undercount recent allocations and believe headroom was exhausted, triggering scale-downs. There was insufficient test coverage for cross-shard consistency during leader handoff scenarios.
hotfix_deployed: 2026-03-11: Backported an autoscaler startup guard that forces leader to validate telemetry window alignment before making any scale decisions. Immediately after the hotfix we restored headroom accounting for impacted pools and increased the safety buffer for burst credits by 20% for 48 hours. Hotfix verification: reduced 429s to baseline within 12 minutes of deploy for all impacted tenants.
mitigation_rollforward: Planned permanent fix: (a) update telemetry router to publish a canonical aggregated stream for autoscaler consumers, (b) add an autoscaler leader healthcheck that rejects premature leadership until aggregation alignment is confirmed, (c) expand e2e tests to include leader-election + burst scenarios. Target release: runtime-1.20.
next_steps: 1) Complete telemetry router canonical stream deployment (owner: telemetry infra) - ETA 2026-03-18.
2) Add leader startup alignment check and unit + integration tests (owner: autoscaler team) - ETA 2026-03-20.
3) Run chaos test job that simulates leader elections under synthetic burst (owner: reliability) - ETA 2026-03-22.
4) Communicate RCA and mitigations to impacted customers and schedule 1:1 follow-ups (owner: SRE/Support) - ETA 2026-03-14.
5) Revisit burst safety buffer policy to consider tenant-level credit variance (owner: capacity) - ETA 2026-03-25.
